name: Normal Traffic
description: Normal network traffic adhering to expected protocol specifications, low error rates, and typical user interaction patterns.

feature_explanation.serror_rate: Low connection error rate indicates healthy TCP handshakes.
feature_explanation.count: Moderate connection count reflects standard network activity.

name: Neptune (SYN Flood)
description: Neptune is a SYN flood Denial-of-Service attack where an attacker sends a flood of TCP SYN packets with spoofed source addresses, overwhelming the target server's backlog queue and causing server unresponsiveness.

feature_explanation.serror_rate: High percentage of connections with SYN errors indicates half-open connections.
feature_explanation.flag_S0: Connection attempt initiated but no response received (classic SYN flood indicator).

name: Smurf Attack
description: Smurf is a distributed amplification DoS attack where ICMP echo requests with spoofed victim IP addresses are broadcast to intermediate networks, causing all hosts to flood the victim with ICMP replies.

feature_explanation.protocol_type_icmp: Abnormal volume of ICMP protocol traffic.
feature_explanation.src_bytes: Large packet sizes sent repeatedly to broadcast destinations.

name: Pod (Ping of Death)
description: Ping of Death (Pod) involves sending malformed or oversized ICMP packets exceeding maximum IP packet size (65,535 bytes), causing buffer overflows and system crashes during packet reassembly.

feature_explanation.wrong_fragment: Indicates fragmented IP packets designed to crash packet assembly engines.
feature_explanation.src_bytes: Exceeds standard Ethernet MTU and IP specification limits.

name: Teardrop Attack
description: Teardrop sends mangled IP fragments with overlapping payloads to a target machine. The receiving system fails to reassemble the conflicting offsets, resulting in OS kernel panic or crash.

feature_explanation.wrong_fragment: Primary indicator of corrupted fragment offset fields.

name: Land Attack
description: Land attack sends a forged TCP SYN packet where the source IP and port are set to match the target's own IP and port, forcing the victim machine to continuously reply to itself until frozen.

feature_explanation.land: Self-referencing packet flag confirming source and destination match.

name: Back Attack
description: Back attack targets web servers (Apache) by sending HTTP requests with deeply nested URL slashes, consuming excessive CPU cycles to process the string parsing until HTTP service collapses.

name: Apache2 Attack
indicators: high count of HTTP GET requests
description: Apache2 DoS exploits memory handling flaws in Apache HTTP server by requesting overlapping byte ranges, causing severe memory exhaustion and thread pool starvation.

feature_explanation.count: Rapid succession of range request connections.

name: Udpstorm Attack
indicators: high count between echo (7) and chargen (19) ports
description: Udpstorm connects a target's UDP echo service to another host's UDP chargen service, creating an infinite loop of generated characters and echoes that saturates network interfaces.

name: Processtable Attack
indicators: high count across management services (e.g. Sendmail, HTTP)
description: Processtable DoS fills the target system's process table by initiating numerous slow connections, preventing legitimate process allocation.

feature_explanation.duration: Connections held open to exhaust system process slots.

name: Mailbomb Attack
description: Mailbomb floods a mail server with massive volumes of email messages or extremely large attachments to exhaust disk space and mail queue memory.

feature_explanation.service_smtp: Mail service targeted with massive incoming bytes.

name: Worm Attack
indicators: rapid count spikes across random destination IPs
description: Network Worm propagation attempts self-replication across connected subnets by scanning for vulnerable open ports and pushing payload binaries.

feature_explanation.dst_host_count: Probing multiple destination hosts to spread infection.

name: Portsweep Attack
indicators: multiple service_ targets from single source IP
description: Portsweep probes multiple ports on a single host or multiple hosts to identify running network services and exploit entry points.

feature_explanation.diff_srv_rate: High proportion of different services targeted indicates scanning.

name: IPSweep
indicators: single port targeted across many IP addresses
description: IPSweep scans a block of IP addresses looking for active hosts by sending ICMP echo requests or TCP SYN packets to a specific port across multiple machines.

feature_explanation.srv_diff_host_rate: Same service probed across many different host IP addresses.

name: Satan Scan
indicators: probing known vulnerable ports (e.g. rlogin, NFS, rexec)
description: Satan is an automated vulnerability scanner that checks network hosts for well-known security misconfigurations and unpatched service vulnerabilities.

name: Nmap Port Scan
description: Nmap scanning utilizes TCP SYN, FIN, NULL, or Xmas packets to detect open ports, OS versions, and firewall rules across target hosts.

feature_explanation.flag_REJ: Connection rejected by closed ports during scan.

name: Mscan Attack
indicators: probing BIND, RPC, and SSH daemons
description: Mscan is a targeted probing tool that scans domain name servers and RPC daemons for specific remote root exploits.

name: Saint Attack
indicators: probing web, mail, and remote access daemons
description: SAINT (Security Administrator's Integrated Network Tool) scans target networks to discover security vulnerabilities for policy auditing or exploitation.

feature_explanation.diff_srv_rate: Systematic assessment across multiple service daemons.

name: Password Guessing (Guess_passwd / Brute Force)
description: Remote-to-Local brute-force attack repeatedly attempts user credentials over SSH, FTP, or Telnet to gain unauthorized system login.

feature_explanation.num_failed_logins: Direct count of rejected authentication attempts.
feature_explanation.logged_in: Indicates login session was not successfully established.

name: Ftp_write Attack
description: Ftp_write occurs when a remote user exploits misconfigured anonymous FTP write permissions to upload executable files or scripts to the target server.

feature_explanation.num_file_creations: Files created on remote server via FTP connection.

name: Imap Attack
indicators: buffer overflow payload in IMAP login command
description: Imap attack exploits a buffer overflow vulnerability in IMAP mail server authentication handlers to execute arbitrary shell commands.

name: Phf Attack
indicators: shell command injection strings in URI
description: Phf attack exploits a CGI script bug in Apache/NCSA web servers to execute arbitrary shell commands on the web server as the web user.

feature_explanation.service_http: CGI script exploit executed via HTTP GET request.

name: Multihop Attack
indicators: stepping-stone connection behavior across multiple hosts
description: Multihop attack uses a series of compromised intermediate machines (stepping stones) to jump across subnets and obfuscate the attacker's true source location.

feature_explanation.num_compromised: Multiple compromised state indicators along network path.

name: Warezmaster Attack
description: Warezmaster occurs when an attacker covertly transforms an unauthorized server into a storage repository ('warez site') for distributing pirated software.

feature_explanation.num_file_creations: Mass creation of storage files on victim host.

name: Warezclient Attack
indicators: large src_bytes downloaded from unauthorized FTP site
description: Warezclient involves unauthorized users connecting to a compromised 'warez' FTP server to download contraband files.

feature_explanation.src_bytes: Large volume of data downloaded from hidden FTP repository.

name: Spy Attack
indicators: covert exfiltration of sensitive system files
description: Spy attack involves an attacker gaining low-level remote access and inspecting system configuration, password hashes, or user data without authorization.

feature_explanation.num_access_files: Accessing system files to gather intelligence.

name: Xlock Attack
description: Xlock attack targets X11 display servers to capture keystrokes or bypass screen lock authentication.

name: Xsnoop Attack
description: Xsnoop connects to an unprotected X-Windows server to eavesdrop on user keystrokes and capture sensitive password inputs.

name: Snmpguess Attack
description: Snmpguess attempts to brute-force SNMP community strings ('public', 'private') to read network topology and reconfigure router devices.

name: Snmpgetattack Attack
description: Snmpgetattack uses valid or guessed SNMP community strings to extract detailed system configuration data and MIB tree parameters.

feature_explanation.src_bytes: Mass extraction of SNMP management variables.

name: Httptunnel Attack
indicators: encapsulated non-HTTP protocol inside HTTP POST requests
high duration with continuous bidirectional bytes
description: Httptunnel encapsulates unauthorized protocol traffic (e.g. SSH, Telnet) inside HTTP requests to bypass strict perimeter firewall rules.

feature_explanation.service_http: Covert tunnel operating over HTTP port 80.

name: Sendmail Attack
indicators: malformed buffer string in SMTP 'DEBUG' or 'WIZ' command
description: Sendmail attack exploits vulnerabilities in older Sendmail MTAs to execute shell commands as the mail superuser.

name: Named Attack
indicators: DNS cache poisoning or buffer overflow in BIND named daemon
description: Named attack targets DNS BIND daemons with malformed TSIG or IQUERY requests to achieve remote code execution.

name: Buffer Overflow (User to Root)
description: User-to-Root Buffer Overflow occurs when a local unprivileged user exploits a setuid root binary's memory bounds checking to spawn a root shell.

name: Rootkit Attack
description: Rootkit attack replaces core system binaries (e.g. ls, ps, netstat) or loads malicious kernel modules to maintain persistent stealth root access.

feature_explanation.root_shell: Root shell active during rootkit installation.
feature_explanation.num_file_creations: Trojaned binaries or kernel drivers created.

name: Loadmodule Attack
description: Loadmodule exploits vulnerabilities in OS kernel module loading utilities (insmod/modprobe) to load arbitrary malicious code into kernel space.

feature_explanation.root_shell: Kernel module load resulting in root shell.

name: Perl Attack
indicators: execution of setuid Perl script with environment variable manipulation
description: Perl U2R attack manipulates setuid Perl scripts (e.g., via PERL5LIB environment variable) to execute arbitrary commands with superuser privileges.

feature_explanation.root_shell: Privilege escalation executed via setuid script.

name: Sqlattack Attack
indicators: SQL injection leading to OS command execution (xp_cmdshell)
description: Sqlattack uses database SQL injection vulnerabilities to break out of the database engine and execute system root commands on the underlying host OS.

feature_explanation.service_sql_net: Database network protocol exploited for OS access.

name: Xterm Attack
indicators: exploiting setuid xterm window title sequence bug
description: Xterm attack exploits a font handling or terminal escape sequence vulnerability in the setuid xterm binary to gain root access.

feature_explanation.root_shell: Terminal escape sequence granting root shell.

name: Ps Attack
indicators: race condition in setuid ps utility /proc parsing
description: Ps attack exploits a race condition in setuid process status binaries to overwrite system configuration files and elevate permissions to root.

feature_explanation.root_shell: Race condition exploit yielding root shell.

name: Ransomware Command & Control (C2)
indicators: encrypted payload stream on non-standard ports
description: Ransomware C2 traffic consists of outbound beaconing connections from an infected enterprise host to an external command-and-control server to report encryption keys and receive execution commands.

feature_explanation.dst_host_count: Single host reaching out to external IP infrastructure.

name: Data Exfiltration Over DNS / HTTPS
indicators: unusually high frequency of subdomains or POST payloads
description: Data Exfiltration involves stealthily transferring confidential organization data out of the network perimeter by chunking data into DNS queries or encrypted HTTPS POST requests.

feature_explanation.src_bytes: Large volume of stolen data egressing the network.
